ATLAS METHODS STUDIO / WORLD 01

Run history a hundred times.

Angkor Mandala Lab v0.1: an uncalibrated agent-based model, evaluated under 100 independently seeded random worlds per scenario. Study stochastic variation, policy contrasts, and why mechanisms matter.

Research warning. These distributions describe a deliberately simplified simulation. They are not probability forecasts about real Angkor. The geographical cells, population capacity, and fiscal rules have not been calibrated to historical evidence. The model does not contain a real military or dynastic-collapse mechanism.

What did the policy change?

The outcome named post-1300 population decline means the synthetic population is smaller in 1500 than in 1300. It is a defined classroom indicator, not a model of Angkor's actual political collapse. For the “no water” ablation, the engineered-water condition measure is not interpretable because that mechanism has been switched off.

Classroom sequence

Exercise 1: Pick one seed. Describe the rise and any decline. Now change seeds ten times. Which story survives?

Exercise 2: Hold the seed constant, compare Reference with Canal-first and Maintenance. Which changes persist across the full distribution?

Exercise 3: Discuss whether differences come from random shocks, assumed parameter values, or model structure. Identify a model strut you would test next.

Exercise 4: Compare the estimated probability of the defined decline event to its observed frequency. Explain why one is conditional on this model and the other would require independent historical calibration.

Python source, complete raw data, paired-run effects, figures and class notebook are included in the archive. Fixed seed set 0–99. Model rules run from year 750 to 1500 without hardcoded imperial founding or collapse dates.
